page: OVHcloud c3-32 is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs on an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor running at 2.3 GHz. The hardware allocation is strictly dedicated with one thread per core, meaning hyperthreading is disabled. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. Local storage consists of a bundled 400 GB NVMe SSD, and the network interface delivers a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps along with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

In benchmark evaluations, the c3-32 demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance, scoring 3078.98 in stress-ng single-core tests, which places it in the top 25 percent of tested instances. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is also highly efficient at 215.28 GB/sec, and text processing via Geekbench scores in the top tier at 2637.0. Memory subsystem performance is robust, highlighted by a strong PassMark memory score of 2939.48. However, multi-core CPU performance, large-block memory bandwidth, and software compilation tasks fall within the average range. For machine learning workloads, text generation with a small 135M model is strong at 283.36 tokens/sec, though prompt processing and larger model inference remain average.

The server offers a balanced qualitative cost-efficiency profile for compute-heavy workloads that do not require hyperthreading. The dedicated core model ensures consistent execution without resource contention, though the 2.0 GB of RAM per core represents a potential tradeoff for memory-intensive applications. Lacking GPU acceleration, it is not suited for large-scale deep learning training. The c3-32 is highly appropriate for single-threaded execution tasks, text processing pipelines, lightweight LLM text generation, and compute-bound workloads such as web serving and database operations.
